spatial_claims.claim: D is a point taken within (inside) circle ABC
DA, DB, DC are straight lines from D to points on the circle with DA = DB = DC
D and E are distinct points (both inside the circle)
The line through D and E produced in both directions meets the circle, forming a diameter through D
D is a non-center point on a diameter of the circle (satisfying the hypothesis of 3.7)

configuration_map: Point D: inside circle ABC (Step 1), on a diameter of the circle (Step 4), not the center (Step 2 assumption). Point E: center of circle ABC (Step 3), on the same diameter as D, distinct from D. The diameter is constructed by joining D to E and extending to meet the circle on both sides. Since the line passes through E (the center), it is a genuine diameter. D lies on this diameter but is not the center, satisfying the hypothesis of Proposition 3.7.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof correctly identifies D as a non-center point on a diameter (constructed through D and center E), which satisfies the hypothesis of Proposition 3.7. The conclusion of 3.7 (only two equal lines from such a point to the circle) validly contradicts the given hypothesis of three equal lines. No angle decomposition, betweenness, or inside/outside inconsistency is present.
